reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but the new range consumer independently implements daily occurrence filtering.

duplication.why: Daily nonworking-day filtering is repeated between shared scheduling and the range handler, while adjustment gating remains repeated across consumers.

placement.why: Holiday recognition belongs in shared scheduling, but schedule policy also lives in the server range handler and a budget-local wrapper.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range endpoint, configuration plumbing, and corresponding tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several occurrence-processing implementations because no shared definition owns the complete skip-or-move policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts independently applies daily filtering instead of sharing the policy implemented in shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange reshapes getNextDate's daily nonworking-day exclusion into a map returning null, and budget/getScheduleDate wraps adjustment gating still implemented in the scheduling consumers.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate adds daily-specific filtering and movement exclusion; getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates, and budget/getScheduleDate retain separate occurrence-policy paths.
